case_studies.title: Generative Compilation: On-the-Fly Compiler Feedback as AI Generates Code
case_studies.abstract: Languages with rich static semantics, such as Rust, provide stronger guarantees for AI-generated code, but their strictness makes generation more difficult. Off-the-shelf compilers can provide useful feedback post-generation, but does not guide intermediate generation steps, such as those during autoregressive LLM decoding. Constrained decoding intervenes earlier by rejecting invalid tokens during sampling, but requires white-box model access and costly reimplementation for semantic constraints.We introduce generative compilation, the first approach to obtaining compiler feedback on partial pr
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of generating reliable code using AI by introducing a new approach called generative compilation, which provides on-the-fly compiler feedback as the AI generates code, resulting in more robust and error-free code generation. The researchers built a system that integrates compiler feedback into the AI code generation process. This has the potential to improve the reliability of AI-generated code in programming languages like Rust.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage AI-powered code generation systems, here is what to do: review your current code generation workflow to see if integrating compiler feedback can improve code reliability, consider adopting generative compilation techniques, and assess the potential benefits for your organization's specific use cases.
case_studies.score_reasoning: While not directly affecting daily infrastructure management, the paper touches upon compiler feedback and LLM decoding. IT engineers might find novelty in the approach.

case_studies.title: Learning Engagement Assistant (LEA): Cross-Course Scalability and Classroom Evaluation of an Agentic AI Tutoring System
case_studies.abstract: This paper is an extension of a paper presented at the ICAART 2026 conference, which introduced LEA (Learning Engagement Assistant), an adaptive AI tutoring agent combining course-specific Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with structured Knowledge Component (KC) models across integrated Chat, Tutor, and Quiz modes. That prior work validated LEA on a single STEM course (CMP511) exclusively through simulation, using synthetic learner agents. This paper extends that work by reporting the first classroom deployment of LEA with real students (n = 8, CMP511) and the first empirical test of its c
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of personalized learning by building an AI tutoring system called LEA, which was tested in a real classroom setting with positive results. LEA combines adaptive learning techniques with knowledge component models to provide tailored support to students. The result shows the potential of LEA to improve learning engagement and outcomes.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on educational technology and AI-powered tutoring systems, but IT teams in educational institutions may be involved in deploying and supporting such systems.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novelty: The deployment of agentic AI in the classroom is not an entirely new concept, but the scale-up and evaluation provide new insights. Value: Although the classroom deployment is valuable, it's not applicable to IT engineers or consultants immediately.

case_studies.title: Knowledge- and Gradient-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Parametrized Action Markov Decision Processes
case_studies.abstract: In this paper, we study Reinforcement Learning in Parametrized Action Markov Decision Processes (PAMDP), where each decision consists of a symbolic action and numerical parameters. In such settings Reinforcement Learning algorithms typically determine parameters with one-shot estimators, which makes their training sample inefficient. Though in most PAMDP environments explicit but incomplete knowledge (e.g., rules, safety constraints, or expert heuristics) is available, it is rarely directly used to increase the sample-efficiency of training Reinforcement Learning agents. We step into this gap
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of inefficient training sample usage in Reinforcement Learning for Parametrized Action Markov Decision Processes. The authors built a new approach that incorporates explicit but incomplete knowledge to improve sample efficiency. The result is a more efficient training process for Reinforcement Learning agents.

case_studies.title: Oracle Agent Memory as an Enterprise Memory Substrate for Long-Horizon AI Agents
case_studies.abstract: Agent memory is a systems problem for long-horizon agents. Practical deployments require retention of task state across extended conversations, recovery of user-specific facts and preferences across sessions, and accumulation of procedural knowledge from prior outcomes. These requirements extend beyond document retrieval: a memory layer must determine which interactions become durable state, how that state is scoped, how it is retrieved under latency constraints, and how it is revised or removed over time. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of agent memory for long-horizon AI agents by building Oracle Agent Memory, a database-native memory substrate. The result is a system that can retain task state and accumulate procedural knowledge across extended conversations. This research is not directly relevant to general IT infrastructure work, but may be of interest to those managing AI or database systems.

case_studies.title: Internet of Agentic Things: Networked AI Agents for Closed-Loop IoT Orchestration
case_studies.abstract: The paper introduces the Internet of Agentic Things (IoAT), an architectural framework that integrates agentic AI, IoT, cyber-physical systems, Physical AI, edge computing, and digital twins into a unified closed-loop orchestration framework. The proposed architecture consists of cloud, edge/fog, and physical IoT layers connected through autonomous AI agents that perceive, reason, coordinate, and actuate across distributed cyber-physical environments. case_studies.summary: This research introduces the Internet of Agentic Things, a framework that combines AI, IoT, and edge computing to create a unified orchestration system. It solves the problem of managing complex IoT systems by providing a closed-loop architecture. The result is a more efficient and autonomous system for managing distributed cyber-physical environments.

case_studies.title: Fin-Analyst at FinMMEval 2026 Task 3: A Live Hybrid Trading Agent with LLM Specialists and Rule-Based Signals
case_studies.abstract: Large language model (LLM) trading agents show promising performance in equity markets, yet remain narrowly focused on US equities with little evidence from live deployment. We present Fin-Analyst, a hybrid agent for FinMMEval 2026 Task 3: an eight-specialist LLM pipeline over news, SEC filings, fundamentals, analyst forecasts, technical indicators, and social sentiment, aggregated by a Meta-Agent for Tesla (TSLA), and a lightweight rule based three-signal vote for Bitcoin (BTC). On the final official leaderboard (accessed 2026-07-05), Fin-Analyst ranks first of all agents on TSLA with a +13.5
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of limited large language model trading agents by building a hybrid agent that combines LLM specialists with rule-based signals, resulting in a top-ranked performance on the FinMMEval 2026 Task 3 leaderboard. The agent was built to trade on Tesla and Bitcoin markets. This research is not directly relevant to cloud infrastructure management.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on developing a trading agent for financial markets. If your organization uses large language models for financial analysis, you may want to review this research for potential insights. However, it does not require immediate action for cloud infrastructure management.
